title: Improve Weekly Radar report quality and testability
outOfScope: Changing domain stage, ranking, Top5 selection, structural-change rules, or source authority policy.
Adding paid data APIs, LLM extraction, new secrets, or changing secret values.
Writing generated report files to the main branch or changing data-branch retention policy.
Sending real Telegram messages from local tests or adding external network calls to tests.
Changing unrelated Work Items, shared architecture tests, or project-wide governance policy.

sources.reason: Repository Work Item lifecycle, scope, testing, finish, merge, and closure requirements.
Canonical repository terminology and architecture boundaries.
AI Cockpit v2 Contract, Preflight, checkpoint, Finish, archive, and closure evidence.
Current SEC acquisition boundary and CLI dry-run behavior to improve without changing source policy.
Current provider-neutral report input and source coverage model.
Current human-facing Markdown, snapshot, evidence-basis, and System Health rendering.
Existing fixture-driven runtime, report, CLI, and workflow contract tests.

riskAssessment.reason: The change affects human-facing report interpretation and manual workflow execution. The main risks are accidentally presenting unavailable evidence as authoritative, hiding source failures, or making a manual test mutate Telegram/data unexpectedly.
riskAssessment.reviewNotes: The existing runtime already has bounded HTTP and dry-run seams. This Work Item adds reporting and workflow safety within those seams; it does not alter source authority, rule-only extraction, or retention policy.

reasons: Initial Work Item skeleton defaults to Standard until scope is classified.

executionDecision.reason: The user explicitly authorized continuing the current Weekly Radar corrections and testing without intermediate confirmation; scope, acceptance, unknowns, and verification are now bounded.

preReviewWarnings: Only confirmed primary evidence may appear as the Executive Summary evidence basis; otherwise render explicit UNKNOWN.
SEC acquisition diagnostics must remain safe and must not include User-Agent, Telegram token, chat ID, request headers, or response bodies.
A manual dry-run must not send Telegram or mutate the data branch; scheduled production behavior remains unchanged.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: The Executive Summary evidence basis selects only a confirmed fact from an authoritative source; when no such fact exists it renders an explicit localized UNKNOWN message and never cites an unavailable or unconfirmed observation.

SEC collection failures are retained as safe, company/source-scoped System Health diagnostics so SEC 0/10 coverage has an actionable explanation without exposing credentials, headers, or response bodies.
Source coverage distinguishes an optional source that is NOT_CONFIGURED from a configured source that is UNAVAILABLE; this distinction is visible in the report and preserved in the snapshot.

Telegram output is a human-first localized weekly report: default Chinese, with selectable Japanese and English; it does not expose source_* identifiers, raw status labels, coverage fractions, or long ungrouped diagnostic lists.
Source and fact gaps are summarized by readable source/company impact and only actionable exceptions are shown; the snapshot retains the complete deterministic fact/review detail.

workflow_dispatch exposes a safe dry-run input, an optional explicit as-of date, and a language choice; dry-run runs acquisition/report validation without Telegram delivery or data-branch mutation, while the scheduled production path still publishes and retains data.
Rule-only extraction, UNKNOWN semantics, primary-source authority, data-branch retention, checkout@v5, and existing Monday 09:00 JST schedule remain unchanged.
Focused regression tests, full project quality, AI Cockpit Finish, archive, PR checks, merge, close, and branch cleanup pass with no out-of-scope changes.
Reader-facing operations documentation describes the localized human-first report, health semantics, and manual dry-run inputs without recording project progress history.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.
Preserve UNKNOWN/UNAVAILABLE rather than inferring missing data.
Keep provider-specific acquisition details at the runtime boundary and keep diagnostics secret-safe.
Resolve defects discovered in this report and test scope in this Work Item; do not create a successor for an in-scope correction.
Use actions/checkout@v5 and preserve the existing data-branch-only publication boundary.

intent.problem: The first successful live Weekly Radar report exposed five reader-facing/runtime gaps: an unavailable Adobe Careers observation was shown as the evidence basis, SEC coverage was 0/10 without an actionable failure explanation, unconfigured Greenhouse/Lever sources looked like ordinary unavailable failures, Telegram review output expanded to 78 individual items, and the whole report was written as internal English diagnostics that a reader could not understand. Manual workflow dispatch also had no side-effect-free test mode.
constraints: Use only deterministic rules and preserve UNKNOWN/UNAVAILABLE; do not add LLM extraction or paid APIs.
Do not change the evidence authority pyramid, source adapters, data-branch retention policy, Telegram environment variable names, or Monday 09:00 JST production schedule.
Keep full detail in the data snapshot while making the Telegram Markdown concise and human-readable.
The report language is zh-CN by default, with ja and en available through an explicit runtime option; localized text remains deterministic.
Manual dry-run must be side-effect free for Telegram and data publication; local and fixture tests must not use real credentials or network calls.
Complete the full AI Cockpit Work Item lifecycle under the user-approved execution already provided.
intent.rationale: These changes directly address evidence-boundary and operability defects observed in the first real report while preserving the approved free-data and evidence-first design.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Evidence basis ignores unavailable and unconfirmed facts.
scenarioCoverage.expected: A report whose first fact is UNAVAILABLE or UNCONFIRMED renders UNKNOWN unless a confirmed authoritative fact exists; a confirmed official/SEC fact is selected when present.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run focused renderer tests with ordered known, unavailable, and unconfirmed fixtures and inspect the exact Markdown.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: SEC acquisition failure is visible and secret-safe.
scenarioCoverage.expected: A failed SEC request produces a bounded source-health diagnostic with company and source family, but no User-Agent, token, chat ID, headers, or body.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Use fixture HTTP failures, render the resulting report, and assert the safe diagnostic plus absence of secret markers.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Optional source configuration status is distinct from request failure.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Unconfigured Greenhouse/Lever coverage is labeled NOT_CONFIGURED; a configured but failed endpoint remains UNAVAILABLE.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Use the existing registry/source fixtures and assert both coverage labels in Markdown and snapshot JSON.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Telegram review output is bounded while snapshot detail is complete.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The Markdown contains grouped review counts and at most a bounded number of examples; the snapshot still contains all normalized facts and the full review item list.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Render a fixture with more than the display limit and assert bounded Markdown plus complete serialized health review items.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Localized human-first report is readable by default and selectable by language.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The default report is Chinese; ja and en are deterministic alternatives. Human-facing Markdown uses readable labels and omits source_* identifiers, raw status labels, coverage fractions, and unbounded diagnostics.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run CLI/report tests for zh-CN, ja, and en, assert the localized headings and absence of internal diagnostic markers, then inspect the rendered fixture.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Manual workflow dry-run is side-effect safe and scheduled production remains intact.
scenarioCoverage.expected: workflow_dispatch declares dry_run and as_of inputs; dry-run passes --dry-run and skips data publication checks/push while schedule still uses 0 0 * * 1 and production publishes PUBLISHED output.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run workflow text regression tests, local CLI dry-run tests, cargo quality, and inspect the final workflow diff.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Preflight, checkpoints, Finish, archive, PR checks, hosted checks, merge, close, and branch/worktree cleanup succeed.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run the canonical Make targets and inspect local/remote branch and Work Item archive state before reporting completion.
